CLASS 38 · AGES 4–5 · 35 FEELINGS & KINDNESS LESSONS

Feelings & Kindness.

HOW THIS CLASS WORKS

Thirty-five cards, four words each, one kinder vocabulary.

Every card in this class teaches four words a four-year-old actually needs: the feeling faces (happy, sad, angry, calm — then the bigger ones), the kind habits (share, help, take turns, include), the calm-down skills (breathe, pause, count to ten, reset) and the belonging words (you matter, I am here, we care). Each card comes with its step-by-step lesson right here — what the words mean, the three ideas your child needs, the parent script, one game for the living room and the moment in your real day where the words already live. The order is deliberate: feelings first, kindness second, the tricky words honestly in the middle, and the choice at the end.

One card a sitting is plenty — the whole class is a term of five-minute feelings talks. The vocabulary is the one early-years teachers use in the US, Canada, Australia and New Zealand: social-emotional learning, emotion vocabulary, feelings check-ins and calm-down skills — the same words preschools teach as the heart of the early curriculum. By the last card, your child holds a whole vocabulary for the weather inside — and the standing rule that kindness is a choice, freely made, every time.

WHY FEELINGS FIRST

A feeling with a name is a feeling with a door.

The research keeps landing in the same place: children who can name their feelings need fewer meltdowns to say the same thing, recover faster when the storm lands and ask for help sooner. This class does not train happiness — every feeling on these cards is allowed, from lonely to jealous to embarrassed. It hands your child the words for ALL of them, plus the calm-down skills that make the big ones survivable and the kindness habits that make other people glad your child came.

And the class keeps its place in the Learning Path honestly: it grew out of Class 32 (Life Skills & Good Habits) — the habits shelf — and it is the older cousin of the first feeling faces your child met in the toddler years. Class 32 points here as its next step; the age-two Emotions & Feelings class remains the gentle way in for younger siblings.

KIND ACTIONS

Kind actions: manners.

Feeling words grow into kind actions — and the Manners flashcards print them: thirty-two good-manners cards for ages 3–5, from gentle hands and offer-to-share to cheering for others, every card carrying a practice tip, a download button and a print button on one free page. Naming feelings here, practising the kind version next door.

FROM FEELINGS TO THE PEOPLE WHO SHARE THEM

Class 45 · Family & Friends.

Class 38 grows the feeling words — and feelings mostly happen around people: the sister who shares, the friend who helps, the grandma who listens. The Family & Friends class prints those people as cards: thirty-five family and friends flashcards for ages 4–5, every card on the one class page with who they are in a family, one way to make their day today, and Download + Print right under the picture.

TEACHER’S LESSON

How this class is taught.

By the end of this class: your child has met all 35 cards in Feelings & Kindness, said each word with you and tried one small activity from the lesson.

  1. 01
    Welcome

    “Hello! Today we are learning about Feelings & Kindness. We have 35 cards, and we will look at them one at a time.”

    How: Sit side by side with the cards in front of you. Keep your voice warm and unhurried, and let your child touch the cards.

  2. Cards 1–10
  3. 02
    Card 1 · Happy, Sad, Angry & Calm

    “Happy looks like this! Sad looks like this. Angry looks like this — eyebrows down! And calm… slow breath, soft face. Can you make all four faces with me?”

    How: Play the four-faces game: you name a feeling, your child makes the face. Then swap — they name, you make the face (an exaggerated grown-up angry face gets the biggest laughs). End by finding the feeling right now: "Which one are you today?"

  4. 03
    Card 2 · Kind, Share, Help & Thank You

    “Heart friendly, book handed over, small friend helped up and a big warm thank you — four kind words your child can say AND do before lunch.”

    How: Catch the words in the wild today: "You SHARED your crackers — that was kind!" "Thank you for HELPING me." Naming the act the moment it happens teaches the word faster than any drill.

  5. 04
    Card 3 · Excited, Worried, Surprised & Proud

    “Excited is when your body goes wiggle-wiggle! Worried is when your tummy feels tight. Surprised is when your mouth goes OH. And proud is when you stand tall like this.”

    How: Act all four with the whole body: wiggle for excited, hug your own arms for worried, jump-back-OH for surprised, tall-stack for proud. Then hunt them in a book: "Find the surprised face!"

  6. 05
    Card 4 · Listen, Gentle, Take Turns & Kind Words

    “Listen means ears open, mouth waiting. Gentle means soft hands with people and pets. Take turns means my go, then your go. Kind words are words that make friends feel good.”

    How: Practise each one in a minute: listen to one whole song, stroke the pet (or a soft toy) gently, take three turns rolling a ball, and say one kind word each at dinner.

  7. 06
    Card 5 · Breathe, Brave, Try Again & I Can Do It

    “First we breathe — in like a flower, out like a candle. Then we think brave. Then we try again. And we say it together: I can do it.”

    How: Pick one wobbly thing today — a big slide, a new food, a tricky puzzle — and walk the ladder out loud: breathe, brave, try again, I can do it. Cheering allowed and encouraged.

  8. 07
    Card 6 · Smile, Care, Forgive & Friend

    “A smile says hello, I am friendly. Care means I notice when you are sad. Forgive means we start again after a fight. And a friend is someone we smile at, care for and forgive.”

    How: Play the mend-it game with toys: two puppets squabble, one says sorry, the other says "I forgive you" — then they play again. Children rehearse mending long before they need it for real.

  9. 08
    Card 7 · Lonely, Loved, Frustrated & Relaxed

    “Lonely is when you want someone and they are not there. Loved is when someone holds you close. Frustrated is when it will not work and you want to yell. Relaxed is when your whole body goes soft.”

    How: Sort today into the four boxes at bedtime: "When did you feel lonely? When did you feel loved? What frustrated you? What made you relaxed?" No fixing, just naming — the naming is the lesson.

  10. 09
    Card 8 · Patient, Honest, Polite & Fair

    “Patient means I can wait. Honest means I tell the truth, even about the broken cup. Polite means please, thank you, excuse me. Fair means everybody gets a turn — including the little ones.”

    How: Play a waiting game (patience), ask a question with an honest answer built in ("did you like the broccoli?"), practise one polite phrase, then deal cards one-each (fair) — four minutes, four words.

  11. 10
    Card 9 · Notice, Understand, Comfort & Encourage

    “First we notice — ‘your face looks sad.‘ Then we understand — ‘are you sad because the tower fell?‘ Then we comfort — a hug, a hand, a sit-together. Then we encourage — ‘try again, I will help.‘”

    How: Walk the four steps on a real moment: a dropped ice cream, a lost toy, a friend who fell over. Your child plays all four parts — spotter, understander, comforter, cheerleader.

  12. 11
    Card 10 · Wait, Ask, Listen Carefully & Say Sorry

    “Wait — I do not grab. Ask — ‘may I have a turn?‘ Listen carefully — ears on, eyes on. And when I get it wrong, I say sorry and mean it.”

    How: Rehearse the ask: hide a favourite toy, then have the grown-up want it back — your child practises wait, ask, and hand it over with a smile. Swap roles and let them be the asker.

  13. Cards 11–20
  14. 12
    Card 11 · Welcome, Include, Cooperate & Teamwork

    “Welcome means ‘hi, come in!‘ Include means ‘you can play too.‘ Cooperate means we each do a part. Teamwork is what it feels like when we do it together.”

    How: Build something that needs four hands — a sofa-cushion fort, a puzzle, a snack plate arranged together. Say the words while it happens: "I welcome you… I include you… we cooperate… TEAMWORK!"

  15. 13
    Card 12 · Hopeful, Safe, Problem Solver & Kind Heart

    “Hopeful means I believe good things are coming. Safe means nothing here can hurt me. Problem solver means when something goes wrong, I look for a fix. Kind heart means all of it runs on kindness.”

    How: Do the problem-solver pose: hands on hips, "something went wrong — what could we TRY?" List two silly fixes and one real one. Then name the kind heart that did it: "you just solved that with kindness."

  16. 14
    Card 13 · Joyful, Tired, Confused & Curious

    “Joyful is happy with your WHOLE body. Tired is when a yawn sneaks out. Confused is when you do not get it yet. Curious is when you want to know more.”

    How: Do the day-in-four at dinner: act joyful, droop tired, shrug confused, lean-in curious — matching each to a real moment from the day. The acting is the vocabulary lesson.

  17. 15
    Card 14 · Scared, Brave, Shy & Confident

    “Scared is when you want to hide. Brave is when you do it anyway. Shy is when new people make you quiet. Confident is when you stand tall and try.”

    How: Draw the feeling map: which things are scary, which are shy-things, which feel confident? Grown-up fills one in too ("phone calls make me shy!") — honesty about fear is the lesson.

  18. 16
    Card 15 · Share, Give, Care & Thank

    “Share means we both use it. Give means here, it is yours now. Care means I keep you warm and safe. Thank means I saw what you did — and it mattered.”

    How: Run one tiny giving circle today: share a snack between plates, give one toy to the donation bag, care for a tired teddy, thank whoever helped. Four words, four real acts, five minutes.

  19. 17
    Card 16 · Be Kind, Helpful, Patient & Honest

    “Be kind — soft hands, warm words. Be helpful — see a job, do a job. Be patient — wait without wailing. Be honest — tell it true, even the wobbly parts.”

    How: Give the be-words jobs: one kindness mission, one helper job (match the socks), one waiting moment (timer for the oven), one honest report ("who spilled it?" — telling true earns a cheer, not a trouble).

  20. 18
    Card 17 · Forgive, Accept, Respect & Include

    “Forgive means we start fresh. Accept means you can be you and I can be me. Respect means I treat you like you matter. Include means I make room for you — always.”

    How: Play the open-circle game: a toy crowd plays "everyone can join" — the circle literally opens wider each time someone is included. Then practise the words: "I forgive you. I accept you. I respect you. Come in!"

  21. 19
    Card 18 · Pause, Breathe Deeply, Think & Choose Kindness

    “Pause — freeze like a statue. Breathe deeply — in through the nose, out slow. Think — what is happening? Then the big one: choose kindness.”

    How: Freeze-dance with a twist: when the music stops, everyone pauses, takes one deep breath, thinks "how do I feel?" and picks one kind thing to do next round. The pause becomes a habit their body knows.

  22. 20
    Card 19 · Proud, Disappointed, Grateful & Peaceful

    “Show me your proudest tower-walk! Now your droopiest disappointed face… and your softest peaceful one. Grateful hands go on your heart — there it is.”

    How: Share one proud and one disappointing moment each at dinner — grown-ups go first, honestly. End with one grateful thing and one peaceful minute of quiet breathing together.

  23. 21
    Card 20 · Worried, Relieved, Jealous & Embarrassed

    “Let us play the four faces: worried mouth… relieved phew! Jealous fists… embarrassed blush. Which one visited you today — and which one can you make RIGHT NOW?”

    How: Tell one grown-up story for each: a worry that turned out fine (relieved!), a jealous moment, an embarrassing one — told lightly, laughed with, not at. Your honesty gives them permission.

  24. Cards 21–30
  25. 22
    Card 21 · Notice, Name, Share Feelings & Ask for Help

    “First notice: ‘something is happening in my chest.‘ Then name it: ‘I think it is worried.‘ Then share it: ‘I feel worried.‘ And if it is too big: ‘Can you help me?‘”

    How: Build the check-in into the day — at breakfast and bedtime, everyone (grown-ups too) runs the four steps in one sentence: "I notice… I feel… I share… I need…"

  26. 23
    Card 22 · Say Hello, Make Space, Be Curious & Ask Nicely

    “Say hello — big or small, it counts. Make space — scoot over, there is room. Be curious — ‘what do you like?‘ Ask nicely — ‘may I?‘ works better than grabbing, every time.”

    How: Practise on toys first: two stuffed animals meet, one says hello, the other makes space on the bench, they get curious about each other and ask nicely for the crayons. Then try it for real at the park.

  27. 24
    Card 23 · Share the Space, Work Together, Take Turns & Cheer Others

    “Scoot in — there is room! Hold it, I will stack it. My go… your go… and when she lands the big one: YAY, you did it!”

    How: Build a block tower with a rule: only one block each, then pass — sharing space, working together, taking turns in one game. Every wobble gets a cheer from the whole family.

  28. 25
    Card 24 · Kind Choice, Good Friend, Try Your Best & Grow Together

    “Kind choice — I picked kind, even when it was hard. Good friend — I showed up for someone. Try your best — not perfect, just my all. Grow together — we get bigger side by side.”

    How: Name the moments backwards at bedtime: "what was today’s kind choice? who was a good friend? what did you try your best at?" Then one grow-together plan for tomorrow.

  29. 26
    Card 25 · Calm Down, Count to Ten, Use Your Words & Take a Break

    “Slow body… count the fingers, one to ten… now the words: I am angry because… Still stormy? Break time — the cushion is always there.”

    How: Make the calm-down corner real before it is needed: a cushion, one book, one soft toy. Practise visiting it on a HAPPY day so the place feels friendly, not like exile.

  30. 27
    Card 26 · I Feel, I Need, I Want & I Choose

    “I feel… sad. I need… a hug. I want… the blue cup. I choose… the puzzle. Four sentences that start with I — because your feelings and your wishes are yours to say.”

    How: Play the I-statement dinner game: everyone says one sentence starting with each word — I feel, I need, I want, I choose. Grown-ups include one real one ("I need five quiet minutes!").

  31. 28
    Card 27 · Listen First, Think First, Speak Kindly & Solve Together

    “Listen first — both sides, no interrupting. Think first — before the words come out. Speak kindly — even if you are right. Solve together — the fix both people can live with.”

    How: Mediate the next toy dispute with the four steps spoken out loud — you narrate, they do: "listen… now think… say it kindly… what is the together-fix?" Step back a little more each time.

  32. 29
    Card 28 · Welcome All, Be Inclusive, Share Joy & Make a Friend

    “Welcome all — everyone gets a hello. Be inclusive — nobody plays alone unless they want to. Share joy — happiness grows when it is given away. Make a friend — today is a good day for it.”

    How: Pick one inclusion mission: at the park or preschool today, be the one who says hello to someone new or invites the standing-alone child in. Debrief at dinner — how did it feel?

  33. 30
    Card 29 · You Matter, I Am Here, You Are Safe & We Care

    “You matter — exactly as you are. I am here — right beside you. You are safe — this minute is okay. We care — the whole family, all together.”

    How: Say all four on a hard day — a fall, a nightmare, a goodbye at the door. Then teach them as comfort-words your child can offer: to a friend who skinned a knee, to a baby who cried, to you.

  34. 31
    Card 30 · Keep Trying, Learn, Celebrate & Be Yourself

    “Keep trying — wobbles are part of it. Learn — every try teaches something. Celebrate — the small wins too! Be yourself — there is only one you, and that is the good news.”

    How: Hold a family celebration for one thing that was HARD today — confetti optional, cheering mandatory. Name the keep-trying part out loud so the effort is the hero, not just the result.

  35. Cards 31–35
  36. 32
    Card 31 · Welcome, Belong, Trust & Connect

    “Welcome — you are wanted here. Belong — this is your spot, your cup, your people. Trust — I keep my word to you. Connect — we check in, we laugh, we are us.”

    How: Find the belonging evidence together: your coat hook, your cup, your seat in the car, your bedtime song. Belonging is built out of small fixed things — point to each one and name it theirs.

  37. 33
    Card 32 · Notice, Pause, Breathe & Reset

    “Notice — ‘uh oh, a big feeling is coming.‘ Pause — everything stops. Breathe — one slow breath in, one slow breath out. Reset — ‘okay, let us start this bit again.‘”

    How: Play reset-tag: when someone (grown-up included) notices the play tipping over, they shout RESET — everyone freezes, one breath together, then the game restarts fresh. Grown-ups calling RESET on themselves is the best demo there is.

  38. 34
    Card 33 · Care, Support, Encourage & Comfort

    “Care — I see you are having a hard time. Support — I will hold part of it. Encourage — ‘you have got this.‘ Comfort — a hug, a blanket, me, right here.”

    How: Care for the caregiver: when a grown-up has a hard day, let your child run all four — notice it, help carry something, cheer you up, deliver the hug. Children give care brilliantly when invited.

  39. 35
    Card 34 · Listen, Understand, Respond & Forgive

    “Listen — all the way to the end. Understand — ‘so you felt left out?‘ Respond — ‘here is what I think.‘ Forgive — ‘we are okay, let us play.‘”

    How: Hold a two-minute listening date: one person talks about their day, the other may not interrupt, then must say back one thing they heard. Swap. Even three-year-olds can do the "one thing I heard" part.

  40. 36
    Card 35 · Kind Words, Kind Actions, Kind Heart & Choose Kindness

    “Kind words — we say nice things. Kind actions — we do helpful things. Kind heart — we feel for people. Choose kindness — nobody makes us; we pick it. Every time, we get to pick it.”

    How: Kindness hunt: spot one kind word, one kind action and one kind heart in your day — then ask the big question: "what kindness will YOU choose tomorrow?" Answer in the morning.

  41. 37
    Practice

    “Now you are the teacher! Pick any card and tell me what it is.”

    How: Let your child choose the card and say the word in their own way. Teaching someone else is the strongest way to remember.

  42. 38
    Check

    “Can you find Happy, Sad, Angry & Calm? Now show me Pause, Breathe Deeply, Think & Choose Kindness.”

    How: A point, a fetch or the word all count as a pass. If they are unsure, name it for them and try again another day — there are no scores and no pressure.

  43. 39
    Well done

    “Well done! Today we met 35 cards. Let us look for one of them at home.”

    How: End on a win, then spot one of the words in real life today. Meeting it again in the real world is what makes it stay.

Read the script while you show the cards — the say-lines are yours to say out loud and the how-lines are the activity behind each step. Skip, shorten or repeat anything: the class bends to your child, never the other way round.
